extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, students, and researchers preparing manuscripts or bibliographies using AMS citation style
extracted.subtask_short: AMS citation formatting for math papers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for citing references and formatting bibliographic entries according to the American Mathematical Society (AMS) style used in mathematics (in-text citation options, ordering, and sample bibliography formats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose one in-text citation style and use it consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three ways to cite references in-text. Select one and use in consistently in your paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly lists three permitted in-text citation styles (numeric, name & year, alphanumeric); whichever is chosen must be applied uniformly throughout the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers within Brackets (numeric citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers within Brackets. Ex. Mathematicians help improve efficiency of data centers use Markov chains [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With numerical citations, references should be numbered sequentially. If a reference is repeated, do not give it another number; rather, use the original reference number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name & Year in-text citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Name & Year. Ex. Mathematicians help improve efficiency of data centers use Markov chains [Smith2019].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the author's last name and year of publication for in-text citation when this style is chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphanumeric Abbreviation in-text citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Alphanumeric Abbreviation. Ex. Mathematicians help improve efficiency of data centers use Markov chains [S19].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form the in-text label using the first letter of the last name together with a shortened year (or other short year form) when this style is chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography format for Print Book (numeric style example)
rubrics_metrics.description: [#] Author’s name as it appears. Title of book. Publisher, City of publication, Year of publication. Mathematical review number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the AMS-format example shown for a print book when using numeric (bracketed number) citations. Follow order and punctuation as shown and include MR number if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography format for Online Journal Article (numeric style example)
rubrics_metrics.description: [#] Author’s name as it appears. Title of article. Shortened Journal Title. Volume Number (Year of publication), issue number, page range, DOI, mathematical review number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include shortened journal title, volume, year, issue, page range, DOI, and MR number as applicable. The example demonstrates placement and punctuation for AMS-style journal entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering and formatting when using Name & Year or Alphanumeric styles
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use the Name & Year or Alphanumeric Abbreviation in-text citation style, instead of putting the reference number in brackets you will use whatever in-text citation style used in the paper and order the references alphabetically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives an example (e.g., [DL99] J. Denef and F. Loeser, Germs of arcs ... Invent. Math. 135 (1999), no. 1, 201–232, DOI 10.1007/s002220050284. MR1664700) showing alphabetical ordering and AMS journal entry formatting for non-numeric styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the AMS Style Guide as the definitive reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS Style Guide contains the most up-to-date standards and editorial practices used in the AMS journal production system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the AMS Style Guide (downloadable PDF) for comprehensive, authoritative rules, edge cases, and full examples beyond the brief examples on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow AMS graphics guidance where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating/Using Graphics: This guide outlines how to create and use graphics within the structure of the AMS citation style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the AMS guidance for figures/graphics (file formats, captions, labeling, citation of reproduced material) as linked by the guide; details are available in the separate graphics guidance page.
